poor adjective

having little money

also needy, hard up, the poor, helpless, pauper, a poor person

classical

Ter. Phorm. 2.3.16 (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ep. 1.1.25: aequē pauperibus prōdest, locuplētibus aequē (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 363

pauper, pauperis

adjective, third declension, one ending · Declension on Wiktionary

poor, of small means

Not destitute but of small means, “that has only enough for his moderate expenses” (Lewis & Short). As a noun, pauper, a poor man; pauperēs, the poor.

Other words

  • inops, inopis — needy, without means

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 1.5.24: rēs pauperēs inopēsque (Lewis & Short); Traupman 156, 153; Traupman 327

  • egēns, egentis — in want, needy

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 23: egentēs abundant · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Rōmae quidem per sē hortus ager pauperis erat

    at Rome the garden was the poor man’s fieldPlin. NH 19.51

  • rūsticus urbānum mūrem mūs paupere fertur accēpisse cavō

    a country mouse, they say, once welcomed a town mouse in his poor holeHor. S. 2.6.80–81

  • pauperis est numerāre pecus!

    it’s for a poor man to count his flock!Ov. Met. 13.824

See also poor, money.
